competition: South Eastern European Mathematical Olympiad for University Students (SEEMOUS)

problems.problem: Let $f:[1,\infty)\to(0,\infty)$ be a continuous function. Assume that for every $a>0$, the equation $f(x)=ax$ has at least one solution in $[1,\infty)$. (a) Prove that for every $a>0$, the equation $f(x)=ax$ has infinitely many solutions. (b) Give an example of a strictly increasing continuous function $f$ with these properties.

Let $P_0,P_1,P_2,\ldots$ be a sequence of convex polygons such that, for each $k\ge 0$, the vertices of $P_{k+1}$ are the midpoints of all sides of $P_k$. Prove that there exists a unique point lying inside all these polygons.

Let $M_n(\mathbb{R})$ denote the set of all real $n\times n$ matrices. Find all surjective functions $f:M_n(\mathbb{R})\to\{0,1,\ldots,n\}$ which satisfy $f(XY)\le\min\{f(X),f(Y)\}$ for all $X,Y\in M_n(\mathbb{R})$.
Let $n$ be a positive integer and $f:[0,1]\to\mathbb{R}$ be a continuous function such that $\int_0^1 x^k f(x)\,dx=1$ for every $k\in\{0,1,\ldots,n-1\}$. Prove that $\int_0^1(f(x))^2\,dx\ge n^2$.
